The EDS analysis shows that the silica sand contains 97.50 wt% of the results, with 0.0019 wt% of Na. However, the analysis of the agglomerate neck structure shows that the reported results by Lin et al. indicate that the defluidization times were consistently longer than those observed in the experiments. The discrepancy is attributed to the composition, which consisted primarily of simulated wastes in the previous experiment, whereas the study used real municipal sewage sludge in the cocombustion conditions.

Therefore, the exact amount of Na (wt %) on the silica sand surface and in the agglomerate neck structure cannot be determined from the given information.
